{\scriptsize\textit{Notes:} $\hat\alpha$ in percent per month. North America, vintages up to 2010 (FW baseline: within-vintage median fund-size imputation; sensitivity in Table~\ref{tab:fw_imputation_sensitivity}): Buyout 25 vintages; VC 27, of which the 23 with at least two funds enter $U_{v,H}$. $U_{v,H}$: the cross-fund pair-product criterion with equal vintage weights ($q_v=1$); under Theorem~T7 (conditional independence of funds given the factor path, eligibility $n_v\ge2$, fund sizes, and vintage origin, zero conditional mean pricing error, no shared vintage effects $c_v=0$, and unique identification), it targets $\theta_0$ at every horizon, $H=0$ included. L2: squared loss on vintage portfolios (DLP12 at $H=0$), whose target is tilted by within-vintage fund noise and moves with $H$ (matched-vintage 23-vintage VC L2 reported in Table~\ref{tab:iv_comparison}). SE: Bartlett sandwich over vintage years, $S=\lceil1.3\sqrt V\rceil$. Significance stars are omitted in this table: in the EW core Monte Carlo at $H=0$, the nominal 5\% fixed-$b$ test of $\alpha=0$ for $U_{v,H}$ rejects 12.1\% (Buyout) and 10.9\% (VC) of draws (Table~\ref{tab:mc_alpha_beta}); FW joint calibration is not separately simulated; and at 30 years conditional rejection collapses to 0.4--0.5\% for $\alpha$ and 0.3--1.1\% for $\beta$ with 6.4--8.0\% on the boundary. SEs are therefore reported as approximate precision measures only. $^{\dagger}$: estimate on a bound of the admissible domain, no SE. In VC the estimate at $H=0$ sits on the $+2\%$ monthly $\alpha$ bound under both criteria because the criterion keeps falling in $\alpha$; that comes from the 1993--1997 vintages as a group, and without them $\hat\alpha$ is negative at every horizon (Online Supplement Table~\ref{tab:vc_without_1993_1997}). Complete 7-horizon estimates: Online Supplement Table~\ref{tab:u_l2_alpha_beta_all}.}
